requirement: The `habeas` skill MUST tell agents that a new project with little code starts with `habeas-requirements`, not `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`, even though most of its code has no references.
rationale:
The requirement has one obligation. The `habeas` skill MUST tell agents that a new project with little code starts with `habeas-requirements`, not `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`, even though most of its code has no references.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_habeas_skill_starts_a_new_project_with_the_requirements_skill]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It reads step 1 of the bundled `habeas` skill's Workflow section. The helpers `step`, `workflow_steps` and `assert_text` do this. `workflow_steps` takes the skill's "Workflow" section and `assert_text` asserts that the text contains each phrase. The test asserts two things:
- The routing row for existing codebases, or code with mostly no references, points to `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`. This is the contrast case.
- The text says "A new project with little code starts with habeas-requirements, not habeas-bootstrap-requirements, even though most of its code has no references". This carries every element of the obligation: the new project with little code, `habeas-requirements`, the exclusion of `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`, and the caveat about unreferenced code.

If the skill text dropped or changed that guidance, the `assert_text` check would fail. The requirement's wording is not ambiguous. I found no uncovered input class and no marking gap.
